summary:
SARSCOPE is an interactive web platform for exploring changes in water-covered areas using satellite radar observations and a water-mapping AI model developed and trained by our team. Users select a location, compare observations from different dates, and inspect model-generated water maps and change results. Color-coded regional markers summarize analysis levels and help users identify locations that need closer attention.

SAR observations can provide information through cloud cover and at night, making them useful when optical imagery is limited. Our prototype includes real SAR-based model outputs for selected areas, alongside a workflow for publishing and viewing analysis results.

SARSCOPE aims to help researchers and assessment teams investigate possible water expansion and prioritize further checks. While it does not currently provide continuous real-time monitoring, our goal is to combine compatible observations from more satellites to reduce gaps between observations and enable faster updates. Future work will evaluate accuracy and explore weather and river-level data integration to support assessment and warning decisions.
details:
Project Overview:

SARSCOPE is an interactive web platform that helps users explore changes in water-covered areas through satellite radar observations and AI-based analysis. It addresses a practical question: where has water coverage changed, and which locations need closer investigation?

Cloud cover can limit optical satellite observations during storms. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can observe through clouds and at night, providing another way to investigate changing surface conditions. SARSCOPE brings observations and analysis results together in an interface that makes them easier to explore by location.

HOW IT WORKS

Our system has three main components: Observe, Understand, and Detect.

Observe: We work with real SAR observations and compare the same area across different dates. ASF Vertex supports our satellite data discovery workflow. Selecting suitable observations requires attention to geographic coverage, product type, observation geometry, and radar channels.

Understand: Users explore an interactive globe or map, select a location, and compare available before-and-after images. They can review observation dates and result information, switch to a change image, and expand it for closer inspection.

Detect: Our team developed and trained a water-mapping AI model. We use model outputs to map water-covered areas and investigate possible changes between observations. The platform includes real SAR-based model results for selected areas. Red, orange, and green regional markers summarize relative analysis levels so users can identify locations that deserve attention. These markers describe the available analysis rather than guarantee current safety or constitute official warnings.

DATA AND TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

The analysis workflow runs outside the browser. After data preparation and model inference, we export before-and-after images, a change overlay, and metadata describing the geographic bounds, observation dates, source identifiers, and model version. A publishing workflow validates and uploads the result bundle to private Supabase storage.

When a user selects coordinates, the server looks for a published result whose geographic bounds contain that point and returns temporary image access links. Selecting a location retrieves an available result rather than starting a new model run or downloading raw satellite files. Available coverage depends on the observations and results that have been processed and published.

We built the website with React, JavaScript, Vite, and MapLibre GL. Vercel hosts the application, Supabase supports result storage, and Python with PyTorch supports model inference and result export. NASA NISAR mission resources support our understanding of radar observation opportunities and limitations. NASA Blue Marble imagery supports the globe visualization. Mission references and visualization imagery are distinct from the actual sensor products and training datasets used for analysis, which are credited separately in the submission's resource fields.

CREATIVITY AND INTENDED IMPACT

Our contribution combines a team-trained water-mapping model with location-based result exploration and regional visual indicators. Users can move from an overview of available regional results to a comparison of observations and a closer inspection of the change image within the same website.

The intended users include researchers, mapping teams, and local assessment teams. SARSCOPE can help them review possible water expansion, narrow down areas for field investigation, and compare conditions across observation dates. Future integration with roads, buildings, and land-use information could provide additional context for assessing potentially affected places.

Longer term, combining water-change observations with weather forecasts and river-level information could support earlier assessment and warning decisions in coordination with responsible authorities. This is a development goal, not a currently validated evacuation-warning capability.

LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

Water coverage changes do not by themselves establish flood cause, water depth, or damage severity. Radar analysis can contain errors, and observation gaps and data-delivery delays limit the timeliness of results. Real model outputs demonstrate implementation, but independent validation is still needed before claiming operational accuracy or measured benefits.

Our next goals are to expand training data across more regions and conditions, integrate compatible observations from additional SAR sources, and automate processing as new observations arrive. We will evaluate model performance against reference data and test whether users can correctly interpret the results. These steps are intended to improve reliability, reduce observation gaps, and enable faster updates toward near-real-time monitoring where observation availability permits.

TEAM AND AI ASSISTANCE

Team404 consists of Minjae Kweon and Hyunwoo Lee. Our project work covers data preparation, AI model integration and evaluation, web mapping, and result publication.

We used ChatGPT/Codex to assist with software development and debugging, interface refinement, and drafting and editing project and presentation text. Our team developed and trained the water-mapping model. Generative AI assistance did not provide satellite observations or independently validate model results.
